facts.problem: some booked customers don't turn up, so a barber's chair sits empty at a busy time
facts.cause: the only confirmation is an email sent at booking, often days earlier, and it gets buried under other notifications
facts.solution: a text the day before that the customer can reply to if they can't make it
facts.outcome: when someone replies, the shop can offer that chair time to someone on the walk-in list

missing_primitives.name: walk_in_list
missing_primitives.why: The catalogue has no walk-in list. One `person` (present) stands in for someone on the list, and the dashed connection label names the list.

checks: Facts come only from the brief. There are no digits, prices, times of day, stats or customer quotes, and none of the forbidden words.
All six essential facts are present, so there are no questions.
The narration is drafted at 30 words in total (9 + 6 + 15), in the owner's voice, and keeps 'can' for the outcome.
Timing: the last-word events are cut back. The checklist is gone, and the walk-in person is drawn on 'offer', so only the connection lands on the final word 'walk-in'.
Show, don't label: a real chair, phone, calendar and person. No steps diagram is used.
Each thing is drawn once. The email, text and reply are all messages on the one phone.
The outcome is shown only as possible: the calendar goes to 'available' (not rebooked), the chair stays 'empty', and the walk-in has a dashed link only.
Four objects. The 2x1 chair and the 1x2 phone carry the story; the person and calendar are 1x1.
No overlaps: chair r1c1-r1c2, phone r1c3-r2c3, person r3c1, calendar r3c3. r2c1 is free between the chair and the person for the 'Walk-in list' label, and r2c2 and r3c2 are also free.
The callout is on the chair, which sits in row 1.
Every 'on' word is copied from its own chapter's narration: chair, empty, busy, email, buried, text, before, Reply, can, offer, walk-in.
Each object is drawn before it is changed or connected.
Text limits: kickers up to 20, headline lines up to 20, callout 22, messages up to 32, connection label 12.
No em or en dashes are used.
